title: BACE: Applied Mathematics - BACE - Applied Mathematics - Unit Conversions
subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: A protocol requires adding **450 $\mu$L** of buffer to a tube. How many **milliliters (mL)** is this?
questions.explain: There are 1,000 microliters ($\mu$L) in 1 milliliter (mL). To convert $\mu$L to mL, divide by 1,000: $$ \frac{450}{1000} = 0.45 \text{ mL} $$
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: Which micropipette would be most accurate for measuring **150 $\mu$L**?
questions.explain: The P200 pipettor has a range of 20–200 $\mu$L. 150 $\mu$L falls squarely within this range. A P1000 could measure it, but P200 offers higher precision for this specific volume. P20 and P10 are too small.
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: A standard curve indicates a sample concentration of **0.5 mg/mL**. What is this concentration in **$\mu$g/$\mu$L**?
questions.explain: Convert both numerator and denominator: $$1 \text{ mg} = 1000 \text{ } \mu\text{g}$$ and $$1 \text{ mL} = 1000 \text{ } \mu\text{L}$$. Therefore: $$\frac{0.5 \text{ mg}}{1 \text{ mL}} = \frac{0.5 \times 1000 \text{ } \mu\text{g}}{1000 \text{ } \mu\text{L}} = 0.5 \text{ } \mu\text{g}/\mu\text{L}$$ The value remains the same.

questions.q: A reaction requires **0.25 M** EDTA. The stock bottle says **500 mM** EDTA. Is the stock concentrated enough?
options: Yes, because 500 mM equals 0.5 M, which is > 0.25 M.
No, because mM is larger than M.
questions.explain: Convert units to compare: $$500 \text{ mM} = 500 \times 10^{-3} \text{ M} = 0.5 \text{ M}$$ Since **0.5 M > 0.25 M**, the stock is concentrated enough to use for dilution.
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: A mass of **2500 ng** (nanograms) is equal to how many **mg** (milligrams)?
questions.explain: There are $1,000$ ng in $1 \text{ } \mu\text{g}$ and $1,000 \text{ } \mu\text{g}$ in $1 \text{ mg}$. Total factor is $1,000,000$ ($10^6$). $$2500 \text{ ng} \div 1,000,000 = 0.0025 \text{ mg}$$
